clue.text: Applaud international bagging 50

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a sack, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a player who has represented their country is awarded a cap, so an international is a cap
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A national team player is hoarding fifty of something worth cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP holds L to give the answer CLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap is to strike the hands together in praise, which is what applauding is.

clue.text: Reach a sort of pass and provide what is expected

parts.note: to reach a place is to come to it
taken as written
in football a cross is a pass played across the field into the goalmouth

explanation.surface: Arrive at a certain kind of pass and deliver on your promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach a sort of pass' sounds like arriving at a mountain pass, but it is the football sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across, in informal usage, is to deliver or hand over what is wanted or owed.

clue.text: Inspect accounts of car manufacturer close to Detroit

parts.note: Audi is a German car maker

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of Detroit

explanation.surface: Checking the books of a carmaker based near Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to Detroit' reads as a location near the US car city, but it means its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of an organisation's financial records.

clue.text: Overcome with anger, police act outrageously arresting pawn

indicators.note: police arresting someone take them in, so the shuffled letters take another piece inside
acting outrageously means behaving wildly, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: Someone is livid because officers behaved outrageously when detaining a lowly person.
explanation.walkthrough: POLICE ACT rearranges to APOLECTIC, and P goes in after APO to give APOPLECTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplectic is used loosely of someone so furious they seem about to have a fit.

clue.text: Star-shaped figure in manger? Apt, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A star in a manger evokes the Nativity, which seems fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentagram is a five-pointed star drawn with five straight strokes.

clue.text: Up amongst legumes — lupins, lentils etc

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading from bottom to top, the reverse direction
amongst means sitting within other things, so the answer lies inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A list of leguminous crops such as lupins and lentils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legumes' looks like the definition but is fodder; the hidden letters read upwards give PULSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are the edible seeds of leguminous plants, including lentils, peas and beans.

clue.text: Terribly dire prospects for camaraderie

indicators.note: terribly means very badly, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Grim outlook for team morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is French for the shared pride and loyalty felt among members of a group.

clue.text: Sober, Paddy had a meal

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper
having eaten a meal is ate

explanation.surface: Someone called Paddy ate a meal while staying sober.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name but is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate, especially in drinking, so it is a near synonym of sober.

clue.text: Cover action

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a protective container or covering
second meaning: a lawsuit brought in court

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover action' sounds like a covert operation; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a casing or holder, and a legal case is an action brought before a court.

clue.text: Name a lake after Italian family that's famous for healing

indicators.note: after tells us the family's name is written first, ahead of the other short pieces

parts.note: the Medici were the famous ruling family of Renaissance Florence
N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A lake was named after a celebrated Italian family known for its curative powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous' seems to describe the healing, but it belongs to the family; MEDICI plus N, A, L gives MEDICINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal describes something having curative properties, used as a remedy for illness.

clue.text: Somehow cheered, met me around noon for a drink

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the extra one
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged afresh

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Somebody, cheered up, met me around midday for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: CHEERED MET ME rearranges to CREMEDEMETHE, and N goes in before THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme de menthe is a sweet green peppermint-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Cat mostly circling mother cats

indicators.note: circling means going round something, so the shortened word wraps around another
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A cat prowling around its mother among other big cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cat' at the start looks like the definition, but the plural at the end is; the first cat is only wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumas are large wild members of the feline family of the Americas, also called cougars.

clue.text: Simultaneously, however

definitions.meaning: first meaning: happening together, in the same moment
second meaning: nevertheless, used to introduce a contrasting point

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works both as a time expression and as a way of conceding a point, as in 'at the same time, it is risky'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means concurrently and idiomatically serves as a contrasting connective like nevertheless.

clue.text: Excessively sentimental story, ripper written about Yank?

indicators.note: written about means wrapped around, so one word is set around the other

parts.note: something that rips is a tearer
to yank is to jerk, pull sharply

explanation.surface: A mawkish tale written about an American by Jack the Ripper.
explanation.walkthrough: Yank looks like an American, but here it is the verb meaning to pull sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-jerker is a film or story calculated to make the audience cry.

clue.text: Polish on river, European one

indicators.note: in an across answer, putting one piece on another means placing it after it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
to hone is to sharpen or polish

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a shine on a waterway, a European one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European one' refers back to 'river': the answer is a European river. 'Polish' with a capital P looks like the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Society member phoned head of embassy in sultanate

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the preceding pieces sit within the country

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
to have phoned someone is to have rung, rang

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of embassy

explanation.surface: A club member called the ambassador in a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternal society, strongest in Northern Ireland, named after William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: An Orangeman is a member of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternal organisation.

clue.text: Deny I featured in awfully rude tape

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears inside it, so the single letter goes within the others
awfully means badly done, so the letters following it are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone denies appearing on a scandalous recording.
explanation.walkthrough: RUDE TAPE rearranges to REPUDATE, and I goes in to give REPUDIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to refuse to accept or to reject as untrue, a formal synonym of deny.

clue.text: Write series of questions about chapter on old festival

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the test wraps around what follows
in a down answer, putting one piece on another places it above, so it comes first

parts.note: to pen is to write
a test is a set of questions
C is the abbreviation for chapter
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Setting a quiz on a chapter about an ancient feast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old festival' tempts as one unit, but old is just a letter and festival alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentecost is the Christian feast celebrating the descent of the Holy Spirit, fifty days after Easter.

clue.text: Washington, for example?

parts.note: surface reading: George Washington, an example of an eminent political leader
setter's reading: Washington is also a US state

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings land on the same word: George Washington was a great political leader, and the answer split as STATES MAN suggests someone from the state of Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a respected, experienced political leader, and George Washington is a classic instance.

clue.text: Distinct touch of comedy by English humorist

indicators.note: a mere touch of something is a small amount, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of comedy
Edward Lear was the English writer of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat

explanation.surface: A recognisable comic flourish from a famous English humorous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: C followed by LEAR gives CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear and distinct both mean easily perceived or sharply defined, without blur.

clue.text: Real teak barge adrift in large body of water

indicators.note: a boat adrift floats aimlessly out of position, so these letters are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine wooden barge floats loose on a big lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Great Bear Lake in Canada's Northwest Territories is one of the largest lakes in the world.

clue.text: Used for corporal punishment, it could make one sweat

definitions.note: a description standing for the strap itself

indicators.note: could make one invites forming the answer by reshaping the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A punishment device that would make anyone nervous and perspire.
explanation.walkthrough: A tawse is a leather strap with split tails, once used in Scottish schools to punish pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawse was a strap applied to pupils' hands as corporal punishment, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: In agreement with a character

parts.note: taken as written
the tone of a place is its character or atmosphere

explanation.surface: Being in harmony with a particular personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A character' looks like a letter of the alphabet, but character means tone.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at one with someone is to be in harmony or full accord with them.

clue.text: Boast about rank

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for circa, about
a rank is a row or line

explanation.surface: Bragging about one's status or position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boast about rank' reads as showing off one's seniority; about is circa, abbreviated C.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag triumphantly, like a cockerel's loud call.

clue.text: Send watch back?

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a timer is a device that watches the time

explanation.surface: Should I return the wristwatch I bought?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' reads as one phrase about returning goods, but 'back' is the reversal signal alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send money or documents to someone, typically as payment.

clue.text: Snoopy's confidant in lumber with store

indicators.note: with means together alongside, so one piece is written next to the other

parts.note: lumber is timber, cut wood
a store of goods is stock

explanation.surface: A timber yard stocks wood, with a cartoon reference thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Peanuts comic strip, Snoopy is the beagle and his little yellow bird friend is called Woodstock.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock is the small yellow bird who is Snoopy's closest friend in Charles Schulz's Peanuts strip.

clue.text: Fabric shrink? So far, both ends of tie!

parts.note: to wince is to shrink back in pain or distaste
yet means up to now, so far

indicators.note: both ends means the first and last letters only, discarding everything in between

parts.note: the first and last letters of tie

explanation.surface: Will this cloth shrink? So far only the edges of the tie have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' tempts as a laundry word next to fabric, but it means flinch here.
explanation.definitionFit: Winceyette is a lightweight brushed cotton cloth, often used for nightwear and sheets.

clue.text: River Don?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., a river in north-east England flowing through Durham
second meaning: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.walkthrough: The Don is itself a river, so 'River Don' looks like one name; split it into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is an English river, and to wear clothing is to have it on, just as donning puts it on.
